executiveDecision: Hold participant dosing and require comprehensive eligibility and safety review prior to further study treatment.
executiveSummary: Participant PT-1042 fails multiple protocol laboratory screening criteria (Hemoglobin, ANC, Platelets, Creatinine, ALT, AST) and has undocumented prednisone dose/washout compliance. Additionally, a Grade 2 AE of nausea/vomiting led to a temporary dose hold, and a protocol deviation occurred due to a delayed Day 15 visit (conducted Day 21). Multiple non-laboratory screening criteria remain unconfirmed.

priorityFindings.title: Multiple Protocol Laboratory Screening Criteria Violations
priorityFindings.finding: Participant PT-1042 demonstrated laboratory values outside protocol screening thresholds: Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL (protocol >=12.0 g/dL), ANC 1.1 x10^9/L (protocol >=1.5 x10^9/L), Platelets 145 x10^9/L (protocol >=150 x10^9/L), Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (protocol <=1.2 mg/dL), ALT 82 U/L (protocol <=45 U/L), and AST 76 U/L (protocol <=40 U/L).
priorityFindings.whyItMatters: Enrolling or continuing a participant who fails baseline safety/eligibility screening thresholds compromises participant safety and protocol compliance.
priorityFindings.interpretation: Participant does not meet protocol laboratory eligibility criteria across hematologic, renal, and hepatic parameters.

evidence.fact: Hemoglobin screening threshold: >=12.0 g/dL; ANC screening threshold: >=1.5 ×10⁹/L; Platelet screening threshold: >=150 ×10⁹/L; Creatinine screening threshold: <=1.2 mg/dL; ALT screening threshold: <=45 U/L; AST screening threshold: <=40 U/L

priorityFindings.recommendedAction: Verify repeat laboratory assessments and clarify eligibility status with the Principal Investigator prior to further study drug administration.

priorityFindings.title: Undocumented Prednisone Washout and Concomitant Medication Review
priorityFindings.finding: Prednisone use was documented from 01-Aug-2026 to 05-Aug-2026; however, prednisone dose, route, and protocol washout applicability are not documented.
priorityFindings.whyItMatters: Prohibited concomitant medications or inadequate washout periods can confound safety assessments and violate eligibility requirements.
priorityFindings.interpretation: It cannot be determined from current documentation whether recent prednisone exposure violates protocol exclusion criteria.

evidence.fact: Prohibited medication and washout requirements must be confirmed against the active protocol.
Recent prednisone exposure ended 05-Aug-2026; dose and protocol washout applicability are not documented.
Prednisone dose, route and full protocol restriction context are not documented.

priorityFindings.recommendedAction: Obtain prednisone dose and route details from medical records and check against protocol washout requirements.

priorityFindings.title: Grade 2 Adverse Event Leading to Dose Hold
priorityFindings.finding: Grade 2 nausea with intermittent vomiting began 05-Aug-2026 approximately 18 hours after study treatment, leading to a temporary study dose hold and oral antiemetic initiation.
priorityFindings.whyItMatters: Adverse events resulting in dose holds impact participant safety tracking, dose intensity, and protocol adherence.
priorityFindings.interpretation: Nausea/vomiting is temporally associated with study treatment administration and preliminarily assessed as possibly related.

evidence.fact: Grade 2 nausea with intermittent vomiting began 05-Aug-2026 approximately 18 hours after study treatment; preliminary investigator causality was possibly related; study dose was temporarily held.

priorityFindings.recommendedAction: Obtain updated AE documentation including final causality, expectedness, resolution status, and re-challenge/dose-resume plan.

priorityFindings.title: Visit Window Protocol Deviation (Day 15 Visit Conducted Day 21)
priorityFindings.finding: The Day 15 visit window was Day 13 through Day 17, but the actual visit and CBC collection occurred on Day 21 due to transportation issues.
priorityFindings.whyItMatters: Delayed visits and delayed laboratory collections create data integrity gaps and may delay detection of safety issues such as cytopenias.
priorityFindings.interpretation: A schedule deviation occurred, delaying safety monitoring by 4 days beyond the protocol-allowed window.

evidence.fact: Day 15 visit window was Day 13 through Day 17; actual visit occurred Day 21. CBC was collected on Day 21 rather than within the Day 15 visit window.

priorityFindings.recommendedAction: Document investigator impact assessment and confirm protocol deviation classification in the site delegation/deviation log.

signals.title: Combined Hepatic and Hematologic Laboratory Abnormalities with GI AE
signals.interpretation: Co-occurrence of elevated liver enzymes (ALT 82 U/L, AST 76 U/L), neutropenia (ANC 1.1 x10^9/L), mild anemia (Hb 10.2 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (145 x10^9/L), and Grade 2 nausea/vomiting in a single participant.

evidence.fact: Four safety events are documented for PT-1042: elevated liver enzymes, neutropenia, Grade 2 nausea/vomiting and mild anemia.
The safety source explicitly states that this is a single-participant observation and does not establish a population-level safety signal.

safetyAssessment.overallAssessment: Single-participant observation of multi-system safety events (hepatic, hematologic, GI). No hospitalization or life-threatening event documented, but cumulative findings require safety review and repeat testing prior to resuming study treatment.
